# @mirego/opencode-forra-attribution

OpenCode plugin that attaches Forra usage-attribution headers from the local git context on every outbound LLM request. With this installed, compatible-API usage is attributed to the current repository and branch without per-session configuration.

## Requirements

- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1 ≥ 1.18.29 (`@opencode-ai/plugin`) or OpenCode v2 (`@opencode/plugin` ≥ 2.0.0)
- `git` available on `PATH`
- A Forra-compatible provider configured in your OpenCode config

## Installation

The same package works on OpenCode v1 and v2. Add it to the `plugin` array in your OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or project `opencode.json`). OpenCode v2 accepts this key and normalizes it to `plugins`. Object plugin entrypoints require OpenCode v1 ≥ 1.18.29.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@mirego/opencode-forra-attribution"]
}
```

OpenCode installs npm plugins automatically at startup. Restart OpenCode after changing the config.

Pin a version if you prefer:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@mirego/opencode-forra-attribution@0.2.0"]
}
```

### Local development (from this monorepo)

From the monorepo root:

```bash
./tools/opencode-forra-attribution/install.sh
```

This symlinks the plugin into `.opencode/plugins/` so OpenCode auto-loads it at startup. Prefer this over the npm entry while iterating — remove the npm `plugin` entry temporarily to avoid loading both.

For all projects (global install during development):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
ln -sfn "$(pwd)/tools/opencode-forra-attribution/src/index.ts" \
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/forra-attribution.ts
```

## Headers sent

| Header | Source |
|--------|--------|
| `x-git-project` | Normalized `owner/repo` from `git remote get-url origin` |
| `x-git-branch` | Current branch from `git branch --show-current` |
| `x-opencode-session-id` | OpenCode session ID |
| `x-api-agent-id` | OpenCode agent name |

Headers are only attached when the provider `baseURL` looks like Forra — the URL contains `mirego.com`, `forra-ai.com`, or `localhost:8000`. Other providers (e.g. public OpenAI/Anthropic) are left untouched.

Git context is read on every matching request, so branch switches within a session are reflected immediately.

## Project label normalization

Remote URLs are normalized to a stable `owner/repo` label (lowercased, `.git` stripped) so SSH and HTTPS clones of the same repository share one report entry:

| Remote | Label |
|--------|-------|
| `git@github.com:mirego/mirego-scout.git` | `mirego/mirego-scout` |
| `https://github.com/mirego/mirego-scout.git` | `mirego/mirego-scout` |
| `https://gitlab.com/mirego/mirego-scout.git` | `mirego/mirego-scout` |

## Override and disable

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `FORRA_GIT_PROJECT` | Override the git-project header value |
| `FORRA_GIT_BRANCH` | Override the git-branch header value |
| `FORRA_GIT_ATTRIBUTION=off` (or `0` / `false` / `no`) | Skip all header injection |

Environment variables are read at request time.

## Graceful degradation

Outside a git repository, or when `origin` is missing, git headers are omitted and the session continues normally. Session and agent headers are still sent when available. The plugin never throws from the request path.

## Development

```bash
cd tools/opencode-forra-attribution
npm install
npm test
npm run type-check
```
